slides.author: Alexey Grigorev
slides.title: Coding agents produce data
slides.subtitle: Token usage, models, tool calls, cache, and project traces are all useful signals.

slides.title: The traces are already there
slides.body: Local coding agents store metadata about sessions. This can include usage, models, inputs, outputs, cache, and project-level activity.

slides.title: Raw JSON is a poor dashboard
slides.body: You can open trace files by hand, but it quickly becomes painful. The useful questions need aggregation, filtering, and repeatable queries.

slides.title: The data workflow is simple
slides.body: Read the trace files, load them with dlt, store them in DuckDB, and build a dashboard for usage by day, model, and project.

slides.title: This is agent observability
slides.body: Start with traces as data. Then add ingestion, schema, validation, and reports around them.

slides.supportingText: Ingesting Agent Traces with dlthub, with Alena Astrakhantseva.
